extraFacts.fact: 316L is the low-carbon grade of 316 austenitic stainless steel (carbon 0.03 % maximum), which is why it can be welded without carbide precipitation at the grain boundaries; it contains molybdenum for resistance to chloride pitting.
extraFacts.source: ASTM A240 / A276 chemical composition limits for UNS S31603

faqs.q: What is the Hexagonal nuts for hydrowashing machines used for?
faqs.a: The hexagonal nuts for hydrowashing machines are 316L stainless-steel hexagonal nuts for the hose end of a high-pressure washer, clamping mechanically on the hose end with no thread seal. They are the coupling nut on a washer hose: the nut holds the hose end to the machine or gun connection and is replaced when a corroded or worn nut needs changing.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the Hexagonal nuts for hydrowashing machines come in?
faqs.a: The listing gives the hexagonal nut as sized to the host equipment, with no part-number table. Send the washer make and model, or the thread and hose bore from the old nut, and we confirm the right nut.

faqs.q: How do I choose the right hexagonal nut for my hydrowashing machine hose?
faqs.a: Match the nut to the hose end and the machine fitting it screws onto: measure the thread and hex across-flats on the old nut, and note the hose bore. The nut is sized to the host equipment, so a model number from the washer saves guesswork.

faqs.q: What pressure does a stainless hexagonal nut for a hydrowashing machine handle?
faqs.a: The listing gives the nut no pressure of its own: it is for high-pressure washer hose, typically 6000 psi and above, and the working pressure is set by the hose and the machine. Never exceed the rating of the hose or the washer pump, whichever is lower.

faqs.q: What is the Hexagonal nuts for hydrowashing machines made from, and where does stainless suit it?
faqs.a: The Hexagonal nuts for hydrowashing machines is machined from 316L stainless steel, passivated with no plating, so its corrosion resistance comes from the native oxide layer. It suits washdown, marine, chemical and food-grade service where a plated steel nut would corrode. The listing gives -40°C to +200°C, limited by the hose and any O-ring.

faqs.q: Which standards does the Hexagonal nuts for hydrowashing machines follow?
faqs.a: The listing cites a manufacturer specification for high-pressure washers, not an ISO or SAE standard. The nut therefore has to match the washer maker's thread and hose end, so name the machine or give measurements when you order.

faqs.q: What does the Hexagonal nuts for hydrowashing machines connect to?
faqs.a: The nut clamps on the hose end and screws onto the washer outlet, gun or extension, with the standpipe where one is used; see the [standpipes for hydrowashing machines](/p/standpipes-for-hidrowashing-machines). It has no thread seal of its own.

faqs.q: How should a hexagonal washer hose nut be tightened and checked?
faqs.a: Hand-tighten the nut onto its mate, finish with a spanner on the flats and check for weeping under pressure, never past the machine maker's limit. Release the pressure before undoing the nut, and replace one that is cracked, rounded or has damaged threads.

faqs.q: Why fit a stainless hexagonal nut on a hydrowashing machine hose?
faqs.a: A stainless nut resists the wet, chemical and salty conditions of industrial washing, where plated nuts corrode and seize. It is used on washer hoses in marine, food-plant and vehicle-wash service.

faqs.q: Hexagonal nuts or standpipes for hydrowashing machines: which part do I need?
faqs.a: The nut clamps the hose end and holds it to the machine, while the [standpipes for hydrowashing machines](/p/standpipes-for-hidrowashing-machines) is the pipe end that the hose is fitted to. A complete hose end usually needs both, so confirm which one is worn.

faqs.q: How do I choose the standpipe size for a hydrowashing hose?
faqs.a: Match the standpipe to the hose bore and to the machine connection it is nutted onto, measuring the old standpipe where possible. Because it is sized to the host equipment, give the washer make and model with the request.

faqs.q: What pressure does a stainless standpipe for a hydrowashing machine handle?
faqs.a: The listing gives the standpipe no pressure of its own: it is for high-pressure washer hose, typically 6000 psi and above, and the working pressure follows the hose and machine. Never run it above the lower of the hose or pump rating.

faqs.q: What is the Standpipes for hydrowashing machines made from, and where does stainless suit it?
faqs.a: The Standpipes for hydrowashing machines is machined from 316L stainless steel, passivated with no plating, so its corrosion resistance comes from the native oxide layer. faqs.q: How is a hydrowashing standpipe fitted to the hose and checked?
faqs.a: Fit the standpipe into the hose end as the hose maker specifies, clamp it with the matching nut, and test under pressure while standing clear before putting the hose back in service. Release the pressure before breaking any joint, and replace a hose end that leaks.
